title: The wall-stack holdout has walls on which it halts
text: For 1RB1LF_1LC1RD_1RA1LA_0RA0RE_0RC---_1RF0LC, Lean proves that the machine halts from the step start with the wall 1 K(24) K(7) K(1), three open counters, for every odd block length from 252 on. In the counter-stack model this is a step where two counts fail together (both would become −2); in 300,819 simulated failing walls the step halts exactly in the 129 cases of that kind, and every other failure runs on. So a failed count is not harmless, the machine has a halting mechanism like the other 3/2-map cryptids, and no set of walls that ignores the values of the counts can be closed without a halt. No halting wall is known to be reachable from blank tape.
